name: Netherlands
note: An adult Dutch citizen who voluntarily takes US citizenship loses Dutch citizenship unless one of three exceptions applies (born and living in the US, 5 years' US residence as a minor, or spouse's citizenship); a US-born child who is Dutch from birth keeps both.
descent: Children of a Dutch parent are generally Dutch at birth; separate loss rules apply to dual nationals living outside the EU for long periods (not covered by the quoted page).
src_title: Automatic loss of Dutch citizenship (Government of the Netherlands)
quote: As a rule, you lose Dutch citizenship if you voluntarily acquire citizenship of another country. There are 3 exceptions to this: You were born in the country whose citizenship you have acquired and that country was your principal country of residence when you acquired its citizenship. As a minor, your principal country of residence for an uninterrupted period of at least 5 years was the country whose citizenship you have now acquired. You have acquired your spouse's or civil partner's citizenship.

name: Belgium
note: Since April 28, 2008 a Belgian who voluntarily acquires US citizenship keeps Belgian nationality; before June 9, 2007 it was lost.
descent: Belgians born abroad after January 1, 1967 who did not mainly live in Belgium between 18 and 28 lose Belgian nationality on their 28th birthday unless they file a declaration to keep it.
src_title: Losing, retaining and regaining Belgian citizenship (FPS Foreign Affairs)
quote: Since 28 April 2008, if you voluntarily acquire another nationality, you do not lose your Belgian nationality, regardless of the nationality acquired. [...] You will automatically lose your Belgian nationality on your 28th birthday if: You were born abroad after 1 January 1967. And between the ages of 18 and 28, your main place of residence was not in Belgium

name: Denmark
note: Since September 1, 2015 a Dane who takes US citizenship keeps Danish citizenship.
descent: Danes born abroad who have never lived in Denmark must apply to keep their citizenship before age 22 (applications from age 20), per the condition noted with the source.
src_title: Dual citizenship (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark, embassy page)
quote: From September 1st 2015, it is possible for a citizen to have a Danish citizenship along with another one.

name: Switzerland
note: Switzerland has accepted dual nationality without restriction since January 1, 1992; a Swiss citizen who becomes a US citizen keeps Swiss citizenship.
descent: Children of a Swiss parent are generally Swiss at birth; Swiss born abroad with another nationality must register by age 25 to keep it (not covered by the quoted page).
src_title: Dual nationality (State Secretariat for Migration SEM)
quote: The right to dual nationality has been recognised without restriction in Switzerland since 1 January 1992 . [...] Swiss citizens who acquire another nationality when abroad do not have to give up their Swiss citizenship unless the other country requires them to do so.

name: Finland
note: Finland has allowed multiple citizenship since the Nationality Act 359/2003 came into force on June 1, 2003; the Act has no rule ending Finnish citizenship on naturalization abroad.
descent: A child of a Finnish mother is Finnish at birth, and of a Finnish father if married to the mother (as enacted in 2003); a Finn who also holds another citizenship keeps Finnish citizenship at 22 only with sufficient ties to Finland (s. 34).
src_title: Kansalaisuuslaki 359/2003, text as enacted (Finlex open data)
quote: 34 § Kansalaisuuden säilyttäminen täytettäessä 22 vuotta: Suomen kansalainen, jolla on myös jonkin vieraan valtion kansalaisuus, säilyttää Suomen kansalaisuuden täyttäessään 22 vuotta vain, jos hänellä on riittävä yhteys Suomeen. [...] 52 § Tämä laki tulee voimaan 1 päivänä kesäkuuta 2003. (A Finnish citizen who also holds a foreign citizenship keeps Finnish citizenship at 22 only with a sufficient connection to Finland. This Act enters into force on 1 June 2003.)

name: Croatia
note: Acquiring US citizenship does not end Croatian citizenship, which ends only by release, renunciation or treaty; Croatian authorities treat a dual national solely as Croatian.
descent: Croatian law provides citizenship by origin for children of a Croatian parent born abroad, with registration conditions (not covered by the quoted articles; original 1991 text quoted).
src_title: Zakon o hrvatskom državljanstvu, NN 53/1991 (Narodne novine)
quote: Članak 2. Državljanin Republike Hrvatske koji ima i strano državljanstvo, smatra se pred tijelima državne vlasti Republike Hrvatske isključivo hrvatskim državljaninom. [...] Članak 17. Hrvatsko državljanstvo prestaje: 1. otpustom; 2. odricanjem; 3. po međunarodnim ugovorima.

name: Slovenia
note: Slovenian law has no automatic loss when a Slovenian citizen acquires US citizenship.
descent: Emigrants and their descendants up to the fourth degree have an easier naturalization route (art. 12), per the condition noted with the source; descent at birth is not covered by the quoted sentence.
src_title: Državljanstvo (Government of Slovenia, gov.si)
quote: Slovenska zakonodaja ne predpisuje avtomatične izgube slovenskega državljanstva, ko slovenski državljan pridobi državljanstvo tuje države.

name: Romania
note: Romanian citizenship is lost only by withdrawal, approved renunciation or other cases set by law, not by taking US citizenship.
descent: Former citizens who lost Romanian citizenship for reasons not attributable to them, and their descendants up to the third degree, can regain or be granted it and keep their foreign citizenship (art. 11).
src_title: Legea cetățeniei române nr. 21/1991 (legislatie.just.ro)
quote: Articolul 24 Cetățenia română se pierde prin: a) retragerea cetățeniei române; ... b) aprobarea renunțării la cetățenia română; ... c) în alte cazuri prevăzute de lege. [...] Articolul 11 (1) Persoanele care au fost cetățeni români, dar au pierdut cetățenia română din motive neimputabile lor [...] precum și descendenții acestora până la gradul III, la cerere, pot redobândi sau li se poate acorda cetățenia română, cu posibilitatea păstrării cetățeniei străine

name: Ukraine
note: Since Law 4502-IX of June 18, 2025, an adult Ukrainian loses citizenship by voluntarily taking another one only if it is an aggressor state's or a state whose citizens cannot use Ukraine's simplified procedure; whether the US is on that list was not checked.
descent: A person whose parents, or one parent, were Ukrainian citizens at the time of birth is a Ukrainian citizen, wherever born (art. 7).
src_title: Law of Ukraine on Citizenship of Ukraine No. 2235-III (zakon.rada.gov.ua)
quote: Стаття 19. [...] Підставами для втрати громадянства України є: 1) добровільне набуття громадянином України громадянства держави, визнаної Верховною Радою України державою-агресором або державою-окупантом, або громадянства (підданства) держави, громадяни (піддані) якої не можуть набути громадянство України у спрощеному порядку, якщо на момент такого набуття він досяг повноліття. [...] Стаття 7. Особа, батьки або один з батьків якої на момент її народження були громадянами України, є громадянином України.

name: Japan
note: A Japanese national who acquires US citizenship by choice, for example by naturalization, loses Japanese nationality automatically; people dual from birth must choose by 20 if dual before 18.
descent: A child of a Japanese parent is Japanese at birth, but a child born abroad who also gets a foreign nationality at birth loses Japanese nationality unless a parent files a reservation of Japanese nationality with the birth notification within 3 months.
src_title: The Choice of Nationality / Nationality Q&A (Ministry of Justice of Japan)
quote: Japanese nationality will be automatically lost if a foreign nationality is acquired by the individual's choice, for example, through naturalization in a foreign country. ... (From April 1, 2022, those with multiple nationality must choose their nationality when they reach 20 years of age if they became a multiple national before 18 years of age, or within two years of becoming a multiple national at the age of 18 years or more.)

name: China
note: China does not recognize dual nationality; a Chinese national settled abroad who naturalizes in the US loses Chinese nationality automatically.
descent: A child born abroad to a Chinese parent is Chinese, except when a Chinese parent has settled abroad and the child acquired a foreign nationality at birth (art. 5), which covers most US-born children.
src_title: Nationality Law of the PRC (Hong Kong Immigration Department)
quote: Article 3: The People's Republic of China does not recognise dual nationality for any Chinese national. ... Article 9: Any Chinese national who has settled abroad and who has been naturalised as a foreign national or has acquired foreign nationality of his own free will shall automatically lose Chinese nationality. Article 5: Any person born abroad whose parents are both Chinese nationals or one of whose parents is a Chinese national shall have Chinese nationality. But a person whose parents are both Chinese nationals and have both settled abroad, or one of whose parents is a Chinese national and has settled abroad, and who has acquired foreign nationality at birth sh[all not have Chinese nationality].

name: India
note: Indian citizenship ends automatically when an Indian acquires US citizenship (Citizenship Act s. 9); the Indian passport must be surrendered. OCI is a visa status, not dual citizenship.
descent: Citizenship by descent requires registering the birth at an Indian mission, generally within one year, and is not open to a child who holds another country's passport (not covered by the quoted pages).
src_title: Renunciation / surrendering of Indian citizenship (Embassy of India, The Hague)
quote: The individual, who has acquired foreign nationality, his Indian nationality gets terminated automatically u/s 9 of the citizenship Act of 1955. So he does not have to Renounce his citizenship. However, Surrender of Indian passport is mandatory for them.

name: South Korea
note: A Korean who voluntarily acquires US citizenship loses Korean nationality at acquisition; dual nationality from birth is tolerated within the nationality-choice system.
descent: A person whose father or mother is a Korean national at the time of the person's birth is Korean at birth (Nationality Act art. 2), and must then choose under the choice system.
src_title: Nationality (Embassy of the Republic of Korea, MOFA overseas site)
quote: Korean nationals that voluntarily acquired foreign nationality must forfeit Korean nationality at the time of the acquisition. ... Those that do declare their willingness to maintain Korean nationality within six months of acquiring foreign nationality will then be eligible for application of nationality choice system as dual nationality holder.

name: Philippines
note: The Philippines allows dual citizenship, but a natural-born Filipino who naturalized in the US must retain or reacquire Philippine citizenship by oath under RA 9225; it is not automatic.
descent: Children of a Filipino parent are Filipino citizens; a child under 18 of a person who reacquires citizenship under RA 9225 can be included (not covered by the quoted sentence).
src_title: Reacquisition/Retention of Philippine Citizenship (Philippine Embassy in Berlin)
quote: IMPORTANT! The Philippines allows dual citizenship (Filipino and foreign citizenship); however, dual citizenship is not automatic upon acquiring a foreign citizenship.

name: Vietnam
note: Vietnam's default is a single nationality unless the nationality law provides otherwise; since July 1, 2025 some applicants may keep a foreign nationality with close Vietnamese relatives and the President's permission.
descent: Former Vietnamese can request reacquisition with the prior conditions abolished by the 2025 amendment; descent rules for children born abroad are not covered by the quoted pages.
src_title: Legislators approve revised Law on Vietnamese Nationality (Government news portal, June 24, 2025)
quote: These individuals may retain their foreign nationality if they meet two conditions, including having close relatives who are Vietnamese citizens and being granted permission by the President of Viet Nam. [...] The law is set to take effect from July 1, 2025. (Also, en.baochinhphu.vn, Aug. 31, 2016: "Viet Nam recognizes that Vietnamese citizens have a single nationality, Vietnamese nationality, unless it is otherwise provided for by the Law.")

name: Singapore
note: Singapore does not allow adult citizens to keep another citizenship: the Constitution provides for deprivation on acquiring a foreign citizenship, and ICA's renunciation route is for citizens 21 or older who have acquired another country's citizenship.
descent: The Constitution has a citizenship-by-descent article (art. 122); its conditions were not captured from the official text.
src_title: Renunciation of Singapore Citizenship (ICA)
quote: A citizen of Singapore can only renounce his/her Singapore citizenship if he/she: Is aged 21 and above; Is of sound mind; and Has acquired the citizenship of another country. (Constitution of the Republic of Singapore, table of contents on sso.agc.gov.sg: "134 Deprivation of citizenship on acquisition of foreign citizenship")

name: Brazil
note: Since Constitutional Amendment 131/2023 a Brazilian loses nationality only on express request (or cancelled naturalization), so taking US citizenship no longer costs Brazilian nationality.
descent: A child born abroad to a Brazilian father or mother is a native Brazilian if registered at a competent Brazilian office, or if they come to live in Brazil and opt for Brazilian nationality (art. 12, I, c).
src_title: Constituição Federal, art. 12 (Planalto)
quote: § 4º - Será declarada a perda da nacionalidade do brasileiro que: I - tiver cancelada sua naturalização, por sentença judicial, em virtude de fraude relacionada ao processo de naturalização ou de atentado contra a ordem constitucional e o Estado Democrático; ... II - fizer pedido expresso de perda da nacionalidade brasileira perante autoridade brasileira competente, ressalvadas situações que acarretem apatridia. (Redação dada pela Emenda Constitucional nº 131, de 2023) [...] Art. 12. São brasileiros: I - natos: [...] c) os nascidos no estrangeiro de pai brasileiro ou de mãe brasileira, desde que sejam registrados em repartição brasileira competente [...]

name: Argentina
note: An Argentine who naturalizes in a country without a dual-nationality agreement is treated as Argentine for all purposes; the agreement with the US applied only until October 20, 1981.
descent: Children born abroad to an Argentine parent can opt for Argentine nationality (not covered by the quoted page).
src_title: Doble nacionalidad (Dirección Nacional de Migraciones)
quote: Argentinos que se hubieran naturalizado en países con los cuales la República Argentina NO ha suscripto Convenio de Doble Nacionalidad. Serán considerados, a todos los efectos como argentinos.

name: Colombia
note: Colombian nationality is not lost by acquiring US or any other nationality (Constitution art. 96).
descent: Children of a Colombian father or mother born abroad are Colombian by birth if later domiciled in Colombia or registered at a Colombian consulate (art. 96; not covered by the quoted sentence).
src_title: Constitución Política de Colombia, art. 96 (Secretaría del Senado)
quote: Ningún colombiano por nacimiento podrá ser privado de su nacionalidad. La calidad de nacional colombiano no se pierde por el hecho de adquirir otra nacionalidad.

name: Dominican Republic
note: Dominicans may acquire a foreign nationality, and acquiring it does not mean losing Dominican nationality (Constitution art. 20).
descent: Children born abroad to a Dominican mother or father are Dominican even if they hold another nationality by birthplace; at 18 they may declare that they assume dual nationality or renounce one (art. 18.4).
src_title: Constitución de la República Dominicana 2015 (PDF on dgcp.gob.do)
quote: Artículo 18.- Nacionalidad. Son dominicanas y dominicanos: 1) Los hijos e hijas de madre o padre dominicanos; [...] 4) Los nacidos en el extranjero, de padre o madre dominicanos, no obstante haber adquirido, por el lugar de nacimiento, una nacionalidad distinta a la de sus padres. [...] Artículo 20.- Doble nacionalidad. Se reconoce a dominicanas y dominicanos la facultad de adquirir una nacionalidad extranjera. La adquisición de otra nacionalidad no implica la pérdida de la dominicana.

name: Jamaica
note: Jamaicans do not lose Jamaican citizenship by becoming citizens of another country, as stated by the government information service; renunciation is a formal, voluntary declaration.
descent: Born abroad after August 5, 1962: citizenship by descent if the father or mother was a Jamaican citizen by birth, descent or registration by marriage on the date of birth (one generation per application, filed through PICA).
src_title: Jamaicans Urged To Get Involved in Political Process in Adopted Countries (Jamaica Information Service, June 2015)
quote: He reminded members of the Diaspora that they will not lose their Jamaican citizenship by becoming a citizen of another country. (Descent: Embassy of Jamaica, Washington, https://embwashington.mfaft.gov.jm/citizenship: "He/she was born outside Jamaica after August 5, 1962, and his/her father or mother was citizen of Jamaica by birth, descent or registration by virtue of marriage to a Jamaican on the date of his/her birth.")
descent_note: Embassy page cited for descent returned 404 on 2026-10-25

name: El Salvador
note: Salvadorans by birth have the right to dual or multiple nationality and lose it only by express renunciation (Constitution art. 91).
descent: Children of a Salvadoran father or mother born abroad are Salvadorans by birth (art. 90, 2º).
src_title: Constitución de la República de El Salvador (Asamblea Legislativa)
quote: Art. 90.- Son salvadoreños por nacimiento: [...] 2º- Los hijos de padre o madre salvadoreños, nacidos en el extranjero; [...] Art. 91.- Los salvadoreños por nacimiento tienen derecho a gozar de la doble o múltiple nacionalidad. La calidad de salvadoreño por nacimiento sólo se pierde por renuncia expresa ante autoridad competente y se recupera por solicitud ante la misma.

name: Australia
note: Australians have been able to take another citizenship without losing Australian citizenship since April 4, 2002; adults who did so before that date may have lost it under old s. 17.
descent: A child born abroad to an Australian parent can apply for citizenship by descent; when the parent is also a citizen by descent, the parent needs 2 years' lawful presence in Australia (not covered by the quoted documents).
src_title: FOI release on loss under s. 17 of the 1948 Act (Department of Home Affairs)
quote: However, up until 4 April 2002, the previous Australian Citizenship Act 1948 (the old Act) did contain an automatic loss provision (section 17 of the old Act) by which an adult who acquired the citizenship of another country may have automatically ceased to be an Australian citizen.

name: New Zealand
note: New Zealand allows dual or multiple citizenship.
descent: New Zealand citizenship by descent passes automatically one generation born abroad; later generations need registration rules (not covered by the quoted sentence).
src_title: Dual citizenship (govt.nz)
quote: New Zealand allows dual citizenship or multiple citizenship — but some other countries do not.

name: Armenia
note: Obtaining another citizenship does not automatically end Armenian citizenship, which is granted or renounced only by presidential decree.
descent: Adults who are ethnic Armenians by descent can acquire citizenship without residence, proving ancestry with a baptism certificate, a foreign document recording Armenian descent, or a parent's, grandparent's or sibling's ID showing Armenian ancestry, plus kinship records.
src_title: Citizenship (Embassy of Armenia in India, mfa.am)
quote: Any person who is at least 18 years of age can become a citizen of the Republic of Armenia if he/she meets the following requirements: Is an ethnic Armenian by descent [...] Obtaining citizenship of another country or unilaterally renouncing the citizenship of the Republic of Armenia do not automatically lead to losing the citizenship of the Republic of Armenia.
